elements.title: Philosophy

principles.name: Kansō
principles.means: Simplicity: leave out what is not needed.
principles.applies: One fact, one home. Nothing repeated, nothing explained twice, nothing you already know. Fewer presses.

principles.name: Fukinsei
principles.applies: The window balances by weight, not by mirror: a quiet sidebar against the work. Hierarchy comes from size and weight.

principles.name: Kokō
principles.means: Austerity: only the essential, the bare core.
principles.applies: One accent. State colour only on what asks for you. Exact Lucide icons, never our own.

principles.name: Shizen
principles.applies: Motion only for live work (the ensō, the shimmer). Nothing jumps or resizes. Light is paper, not white, and reads like dark.

principles.name: Yūgen
principles.means: Subtlety: suggest rather than show everything.
principles.applies: Detail appears when you open or point at something. A stand-in shows only while its home is out of view.

principles.name: Datsuzoku
principles.applies: One memorable element: the ensō, and the dawn that rises once.

principles.name: Seijaku
principles.applies: A calm rest state. One drawing for each piece and each state, so nothing surprises.

why: kansō is named after one of the seven principles of Zen art described by Shin'ichi Hisamatsu in *Zen and the Fine Arts* (1971). The design follows all seven as one philosophy, not taste.
Every guideline on these boards names the principle it serves. A decision that cannot name one is an opinion, and is not taken.
One limit sits above them: kansō removes information, never options. Every action stays one press away.

elements.title: Tokens
elements.summary: The only values kansō may use. Every size, space, radius, height, icon, switch, motion and colour comes from this set.
use: Take every size, space, radius, height and colour from a token, in the app and in a design.
Pick the token by its role, not by the number that looks closest.
Write text in fg, muted or dim only, at 4.5:1 or more on every surface it can sit on.
Change tone on hover, focus and press; never the size or position of a box.
avoid: A raw number or hex colour in code, when a token holds that value.
A new token for one place. Use the nearest role, or ask for the set to change.
A palette value where the published value differs: the published one is the one that passes contrast.
Dawn colours on controls or text. They belong to the Dawn Mode art.

files.role: every token: name, value and role, colour in dark and light
the constants the app draws with: G, H, R, T, ICON, SWITCH, ARM_MS

elements.agent: Use only kansō's tokens. Read kanso/tokens.json for every size, space, radius, height, icon, switch, motion and colour (dark and light), and pick each by its role. In the app, draw with the constants in kanso/mods/kanso-panel/ui.js (G, H, R, T, ICON, SWITCH, ARM_MS). Write no raw number or hex colour that a token holds, and add no new token. Text is fg, muted or dim, and must keep 4.5:1 on canvas, chrome, bg, raised and popover in both themes. Hover, focus and press change tone only, never a box.
